title: Finding who is blocking whom, while it is happening

videos.script: The checkout page times out. Connections pile up. The query behind it is the simplest update in the application. {{symptom}} Its plan is fine. It is not slow. It is waiting. {{waiting}} Somewhere there is a session holding what it needs, and that session is often doing nothing at all. {{idle}} This lesson is about finding it while it is happening. {{title}} You build a chain on purpose: one session that opened a transaction and went quiet, and two more stuck behind it. {{chain}} Then you read it three ways. First pg_locks, the raw list of every lock and every request. {{pglocks}} Then pg_blocking_pids, which tells you who waits for whom, the way the server decided it. {{blocking}} Then a recursive query that draws the whole thing as a tree, with the root at the top. {{tree}} Then you act on the root. Cancel, which turns out to do nothing to an idle session. And terminate, which ends it and rolls its work back. {{act}} Last, one setting that writes a log line for every long wait, so the next one is on record even when nobody was watching. {{log}} By the end you will have two files that answer, in one screen, the first question of any lock incident. Who is at the root? {{end}}
